rows.note: Use 洗 as the all-purpose verb for cleaning something or oneself with water.

example.jyutping: ngo5 sai2 gon1 zing6 di1 wun2 sin1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the act or instance of washing.

example.english: This wash used a lot of water.
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 sai2 saam1 jung6 zo2 hou2 do1 seoi2

rows.note: Use 沖涼 specifically for the everyday act of washing oneself by showering or bathing.

example.english: It’s so hot—I’m going to wash myself first.
example.jyutping: gam3 jit6 ngo5 cung1 loeng4 sin1

rows.note: Use this for a hygienic or medicinal washing liquid or lotion.

example.english: This wash is for cleaning wounds.
example.traditional: 呢支洗液係用嚟清潔傷口嘅。
example.jyutping: nei1 zi1 sai2 jik6 hai6 jung6 lei4 cing1 git3 soeng1 hau2 ge3

rows.note: Use this for one washing-machine load of clothes.

example.english: The clothes from that wash load still aren't dry, so don't put them away.
example.traditional: 一機衫仲未乾，唔好收埋。
example.jyutping: jat1 gei1 saam1 zung6 mei6 gon1 m4 hou2 sau1 maai4

rows.note: Use 沖走 when moving water carries something away or downstream.

example.english: Heavy rain can wash the sand away.
example.jyutping: daai6 jyu5 zoeng1 di1 saa1 cung1 zau2 zo2

rows.note: Use 浸濕 when water or another liquid covers or soaks something and makes it wet, rather than cleaning or carrying it away.

example.english: The rain soaked all the clothes, so I had to wash them again.
example.traditional: 場雨將啲衫浸濕晒，我唯有重新洗過。
example.jyutping: coeng4 jyu5 zoeng1 di1 saam1 zam3 sap1 saai3 ngo5 wai4 jau5 cung4 san1 sai2 gwo3

rows.note: Use this for the wave or wake made by a moving boat, rather than ordinary waves on a beach.

example.english: When the boat went past, its wash reached the shore.
example.traditional: 隻船一駛過，船浪就打到岸邊。
example.jyutping: zek3 syun4 jat1 sai2 gwo3 syun4 long6 zau6 daa2 dou3 ngon6 bin1
